full_judgment: 5. The defendants then preferred Title Appeal No. 357 of 1992 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka. The learned 8th Court of the Additional District Judge, Dhaka who heard the said appeal found that the plaintiff could not prove that the suit land become enemy and vested property or that the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 346 of 1977 was a fraudulent one. The lower appellate court held that the burden of proof lies on the plaintiff to prove that the suit property became enemy property and subsequently vested in the government. The lower appellate court further noticed that fraud and non-joinder of party are not similar and for non- joinder of party it cannot be held that the suit was vitiated by fraud. The learned Additional District Judge further noticed that the plaintiff must prove fraud as they pleaded fraud in the plaint and this not having been proved, the trial court committed error of law in holding that non-joinder of the superintendent, vested and non-resident property has rendered the suit as nullity upon mis-conception of law. Accordingly by judgment and decree dated 30.5.1999 the learned Additional District Judge allowed the appeal, reversed the decision of the trial court and dismissed the plaintiffs suit.
